title: Pacific Coast Recreational Fisheries Information Network Data Warehouse

access.reason: The public SD002 report establishes a technical path to recreational sample records and blank-catch rows, but its default output is not a complete canonical effort export. Raw QueryBuilder exports require an authorized account, and reproducibility and permission require an official saved query or supplied export, dictionary, checksum, and written intended-use boundary.
instructions: Use public SD002 only for discovery; do not automate bulk collection or treat visibility as a license.

Request an official export or authorized QueryBuilder raw query for California CRFS complete sample records, retaining stable sample, angler, catch, and location identifiers and legitimate blank-catch attempts.
Save the query or SQL, filters, export timestamp, data-good-through and refresh values, row count, dictionary version, and raw checksum alongside the unchanged private raw file.
Obtain written confirmation of commercial ML, derived-product, retention, attribution, and redistribution boundaries before normalization.
Preserve state, survey, mode, area, target, species, time, effort, sampling, selection, expansion, QA, missingness, and precision fields.
Only rows with legitimately released point coordinates may enter point-level terrain models.
access.ingestion_command: python -m pipeline.contourcast.cli ingest-observations --input CANONICAL_RECFIN_COMPLETE_EFFORT.jsonl --output DATA/recfin.csv --source-id psmfc_recfin --primary-target-taxon-id california-halibut --expected-sha256 SHA256

coverage: Recreational sample data and estimates for Washington, Oregon, and California; product-specific years vary.
citation: Pacific States Marine Fisheries Commission, Recreational Fisheries Information Network. Cite the contributing survey, query, and access date.
limitations: Data from different state/federal surveys may use different designs and are not automatically comparable.
Expanded estimates require survey-design-aware uncertainty handling.
The public SD002 default report omits stable record identifiers and does not establish that blank catch fields are confirmed zero-catch complete attempts.
The published dictionary documents NUMBER_HOURS_FISHED for Oregon only; California effort units require official clarification.
Public location granularity may be coarser than bathymetry pixels.
Absence of an observed catch is not proof that a species was absent from a location.
